output.brief:
The complaints are most likely caused by water-contaminated brake fluid, not driver technique and not the new pads. All 11 Eastgate vans with complaints were serviced at Northfield Motor Services during the bay closure. Eleven of those 13 vans got fluid from an old bulk drum that had been opened in March and had a missing cap. The two Northfield vans that got fluid from a new drum have no complaints. Two vans were retested on 24 September and the fluid boiled at about 150°C, against 255°C for sealed stock. Drivers who complained also drove other vans on the same hilly routes without problems. That rules out technique and routes as the main cause. Pads on Calder Road vans and in-house vans show no matching problem. The garage warned Larkspur on 25 September and got no reply.

Next steps:
1. Pull every Northfield-serviced van from service now.
2. Test the fluid and renew it from sealed stock.
3. Check the two new-drum vans too, to be safe.
4. Do not discipline drivers. Their reports were accurate, and punishing them will stop people reporting.
5. Treat the pad squeal as a separate, lower-priority question.

I'm fairly confident, around 85–90%. The remaining unknown is how many vans are affected beyond those reported.
